claims.text: High-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings is governed by the formation of a stable protective oxide scale.
Pre-oxidation annealing in an oxygen-rich environment enhances oxide-scale formation on FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
The oxide layer produced by pre-oxidation reduces adhesive wear during high-temperature exposure.
The oxide layer produced by pre-oxidation reduces abrasive wear during high-temperature exposure.
High-temperature exposure in an oxygen-rich environment causes selective oxidation of elements in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Selective oxidation of FeNiCrCoCu produces a stable oxide layer.
A continuous oxide scale acts as a barrier between the coating and the wear counterface.
Reducing direct contact between the coating and counterface reduces adhesive wear.
Reducing direct contact between the coating and counterface reduces abrasive wear.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have significantly lower wear rates than untreated as-deposited coatings at high temperature.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will exhibit improved friction performance relative to untreated as-deposited coatings at high temperature.
The proposed protective-oxide mechanism applies at approximately 600–800°C under moderate mechanical loading.
The wear behavior may differ at lower temperatures or under extremely high loads.
The optimum oxide composition, thickness, and long-term stability may vary with processing conditions.
